segments.source: Yarrow is 1 map unit(s) north of Quartz; Kite is 1 map unit(s) east of Yarrow; Grove is 1 map unit(s) south of Kite; Alder is 1 map unit(s) west of Grove. A museum in Juniper opens on Saturday.
Treat east as +x, west as −x, north as +y, and south as −y. Add the moves in order. A fact that does not affect any coordinate is irrelevant.
Where is Alder relative to Quartz? What is the straight grid displacement measured as |x|+|y|? Identify any irrelevant fact.

1. Start Quartz at (0,0). 2. Translate each relation into a coordinate move. 3. Adding the moves gives (0,0). 4. That coordinate is the same position of Quartz; the grid displacement is |0|+|0|=0. 5. The museum sentence changes no coordinate, so it is a distractor.
Alder is the same position of Quartz; grid displacement 0 unit(s). The museum fact is irrelevant.
Cardinal directions become easier to reason about when they are treated as relations that can be composed.
Grid coordinates; each statement adds a vector; sum the vectors and classify the final coordinate.
Problem 756. The best route from Elm to Willow
A road map can be modeled as a graph. The best route depends on the stated criterion, not on how short it looks on paper.
Elm–Northfield–Willow has segment costs [6, 7] (total 13); Elm–Riverbend–Harbor–Willow has segment costs [5, 2, 6] (total 13); Elm–Birch–Willow has segment costs [9, 4] (total 13).
A route is feasible only if all of its roads are open. The cost of a route is the sum of its segment costs. Choose the feasible route with the smallest total.
Which route should a traveler use from Elm to Willow, and why?
1. List the candidate routes and their segment costs. 2. All listed routes are open. 3. Add the segment costs for every feasible route. 4. The smallest feasible total is 13, on Elm–Northfield–Willow.
A shortest path is a reasoning result: first respect constraints, then compare the remaining costs.
Weighted graph; delete forbidden edges; minimize the sum of edge weights.
